requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill` is a content requirement on a bundled skill. It has one test, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`. It checks the skill text through `bundled_skill`, `assert_phrases` and `assert_text_in_order`. These helpers read `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` through `skill_files`, which uses `include_str!`. They panic with the missing phrase if it is absent.

Obligations and how the test covers them:
- **Bundle the skill.** `SKILLS.contains("habeas-bootstrap-requirements")` is asserted, and the skill description must start with "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase". The same skill text is read via `include_str!`, so the file must exist in `assets/skills`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_are_five_skill_directories_each_home_to_its_topics]` separately checks that `assets/skills` is published and that the skill directories match `SKILLS`. It is marked for `requirements.cli.skill_structure`, so it is context here and I did not reassess it.
- **Read the code and tests.** The test asserts "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and "Follow behavior through the code". Both are present in workflow step 2 of the skill.
- **Map every first-party test to a requirement or example.** The test asserts "every first-party runnable test or test case", "Record the behavior each test checks…", "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example", and "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references". The Inventories and Tagging sections of the skill contain these phrases.
- **Identify and map every source unit that implements end-user-visible behavior.** The test asserts "every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source rather than from the coverage warnings". It also asserts the observable-surface list ("public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors, and distinct observable branches") and "A tagged entry point doesn't mean every observable branch beneath it has a requirement".
- **Report gaps and do not claim completeness without an independent inventory review.** `assert_in_order` checks this sequence in the skill: "recount both inventories from the source and tests without your lists", then the gap-list report format, then "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", then "Don't silently exclude difficult cases". I read the skill. These phrases sit in workflow step 8 and the Report section. The recount is a fresh-subagent step, and the 100% claim is conditioned on the independent recount agreeing.

For a requirement about the contents of a text asset, asserting these directive phrases is the appropriate check. I found no plausible way for the skill to violate the requirement while passing these assertions. Removing the tests-mapping, source-unit mapping, gap-reporting or independent-recount directive would each break a specific assertion. Reordering the recount, gap format and completeness condition would break the ordered check. I found no acknowledged gaps and no gaps of my own.
